clue.text: Green people weep, concealing awful scowl

indicators.note: the word for weeping wraps around and hides the jumbled letters

parts.note: to blub is to weep, informal British

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of scowl are in a terrible mess and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A gardener's crowd cries while trying to hide an ugly frown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' is a bowling green, not the colour or an environmentalist; 'awful' gives OWLSC, an anagram, and 'concealing' hides it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn bowls is played on a green, so its players form a society devoted to that game.

clue.text: Boy that comes second gets a half of his medal

parts.note: B is the second letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: half of a six-letter word is its first three letters

parts.note: the runner-up wins a silver medal

explanation.surface: A runner-up earns a share of the medal he won.
explanation.walkthrough: The second-placed boy's medal is silver; 'half of' keeps its first three letters, SIL, after B and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a common masculine given name, so it stands for a boy.

clue.text: Plump for having underground source?

definitions.meaning: plump means comfortably fat, nourished well
read literally, supplied from a well dug into the ground

explanation.definitionFit: Someone plump looks generously nourished; read literally, the hyphenated term means fed from a well.

clue.text: Not the lot though you say otherwise?

definitions.text: Not the lot though you say otherwise?

parts.words: Not the lot though you say otherwise?
parts.note: the word means a part, not everything, yet spoken aloud it is identical to a word for the total

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a portion rather than all, while its sound matches the word for a total.

clue.text: Want to be extended?

definitions.meaning: to want something badly is to yearn or pine for it
extended means stretched out, of great length

explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to want, and something stretched out to great length is extended.

clue.text: No. 1 reception: it is to be 2, according to 17

definitions.text: it is to be 2, according to 17

parts.note: number one means the best
an at-home is a reception held in one's own house

explanation.surface: A top-class party where, says Shakespeare's tyrant's wife, eating is better done.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 is WELL-FED and 17 is MACBETH: Lady Macbeth says 'To feed were best at home'. An at-home is a formal party given at one's house.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Macbeth's line says feeding (being well fed) is most fitting in one's own house, so the phrase completes her thought.

clue.text: Worthless object with flaws from right to left

indicators.note: reading from right to left means the word is written backwards in an across entry

parts.note: warts are blemishes or flaws, as in warts and all

explanation.surface: A flawed thing of no value is read the wrong way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw is proverbially worthless, as in not caring a straw.

clue.text: Appear holding two articles, one related to jellyfish

indicators.note: the word for appearing holds the articles inside it

parts.note: to appear is to seem
A is the indefinite article
AN is the other form of the indefinite article
taken as the word one

explanation.surface: A creature shows itself carrying two bits of grammar, a cousin of the jellyfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is not a link here: it is spelt out as part of the creature's name, while 'holding' builds SEAANEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea anemones and jellyfish both belong to the cnidarians, so the creature is a relative of them.

clue.text: Shining as moon in desert?

indicators.note: the moon's name sits inside the word for deserting

parts.note: to rat is to desert, as a rat leaves a sinking ship
Dian (Diana) is the Roman moon goddess, a poetic name for the moon

explanation.surface: The moon glows over a desert landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a sandy place; it is the verb, RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiant means glowing brightly, which is what something shining does.

clue.text: Become detached in outlook with inferior surroundings

indicators.note: the word for inferior surrounds the rest

parts.note: worse means inferior, of lower quality

indicators.note: the out in the word outlook says the letters of look are out of order

explanation.surface: Someone's view of life loosens its grip amid poor conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria splits 'outlook' in two: its 'out' is the anagram signal working on the rest, yielding KLOO, which 'surroundings' encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that works loose gradually comes free of its fixing and becomes detached.

clue.text: Pacific fellow I traduce after a day on my own

indicators.note: the I and the slandering come after the day and the solo

parts.note: solo means alone, on one's own
Mon is an abbreviation for Monday
to traduce someone is to slander them

explanation.surface: A man from the Pacific confesses to badmouthing someone after a day alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An islander from the Pacific archipelago east of New Guinea is a Pacific person.

clue.text: Sentence from a biography

definitions.meaning: a ... term in prison, a criminal sentence
a ... is an account of someone's ... story

explanation.definitionFit: A life sentence is a jail term, and a written account of a person is called their life.

clue.text: "23 21 10 3 ___ 24 ___", wrote fellow after 22 14across 4

parts.note: the numbered answers make a famous line by the American poet named by 22, 14 and 4 plus fellow, and the two blanks together fill this entry

explanation.walkthrough: 23, 21, 10, 3 and 24 give INTO EACH LIFE SOME ... MUST ...; 22, 14 and 4 plus 'fellow' name Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, author of 'The Rainy Day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Longfellow's line runs that into every life some wet weather must descend, so the two blanks together name precipitation.

clue.text: Cakes cause revolutions in central Europe

parts.note: Switzerland is in central Europe, so things there are Swiss
a roll is one turn over, a revolution

explanation.surface: Pastries spark uprisings in the heart of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutions' suggests political uprisings; here it means turns or rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiss rolls are sponge cakes spread with jam and rolled up.

clue.text: Hairstyle study by student in craft centre?

indicators.note: the study and the student go inside the craft centre

parts.note: docks are where boats, or craft, are centred
to read a subject is to study it at university
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A hairdo is researched by a learner at a centre for handicrafts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft centre' suggests arts and crafts; the craft are boats and the centre is the DOCKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadlocks are a style of hair twisted into long matted ropes.

clue.text: See 22
Heated preliminary to conflict when crazy Walter captured Robert the rebel

indicators.note: the scrambled name holds the rebel captive inside it
crazy says the letters of Walter go wild and are rearranged

parts.note: Robert Kett (sometimes spelt Ket) led a rebellion in Norfolk in 1549

explanation.surface: A mad Walter seizes a rebel named Robert, heating things up before battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' yields WARTLE, the anagram, and 'captured' holds the rebel. Kett's Rebellion of 1549 is often spelt Ket's in older histories.
explanation.definitionFit: A war kettle is a pot set boiling before going to battle, so it is a heated prelude to fighting.

clue.text: Railway served by Scots police?

parts.note: a whimsical picture of an underground railway linked with Met, a nickname for a police force

explanation.definitionFit: A metro is an underground or urban railway system, like those of Paris or Glasgow.

clue.text: Take birds from twin brother or uncle

parts.note: R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
emus are large flightless birds

explanation.surface: A relative is told to remove some birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Remus was the twin of Romulus, and Uncle Remus told the Brer Rabbit stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to Romulus's twin in Roman legend and to the storytelling Uncle Remus.

clue.text: Scottish king with American subject clasping imperial award

indicators.note: the subject holds the award within it

parts.note: math is the American word for mathematics, a school subject
CBE is Commander of the Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: A Scots monarch with a US topic holds an honour of the Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth was an eleventh-century king of Scotland, the subject of Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Corroboration claimed in process

indicators.note: to process something is to work it over, so these letters are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: Supporting evidence is asserted during a legal action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'process' looks like legal proceedings, but it rearranges CLAIMED and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An adminicle is a piece of supporting evidence in law, something that corroborates.

clue.text: Vehicle at tea party, a wild one

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
a riot is a wildly lively party, a real riot

explanation.surface: A carriage arrives at a tea party that gets out of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot is a two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle used in ancient warfare and racing.

clue.text: Student entertained by enchantress follows directions to go round

indicators.note: the enchantress with the student comes after the directions

parts.note: E and N are the compass directions east and north

indicators.note: the enchantress plays host, holding the student inside her name

parts.note: Circe was the enchantress who turned Odysseus's men into pigs
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A learner, after taking directions, is welcomed by a sorceress to make a circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertained by' gives CIRCLE; Circe is the enchantress of Homer's Odyssey.
explanation.definitionFit: To encircle something is to surround it, to form a ring around it.

clue.text: Per head (heart) at church

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters, here of the word head

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is costed per person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Per head' looks like the definition, but 'Per' alone defines; 'heart' takes the middle of 'head', EA.
explanation.definitionFit: Per means for every one, as in a pound per ticket, so it is a synonym of each.

clue.text: Why was red thorn used at poet's christening?

definitions.note: the clue names the act of naming; the answer is the given names the poet received

indicators.note: the letters of the question are used up and remade into new words

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about a red thorn bush at a writer's baptism.
explanation.walkthrough: These are Longfellow's first and middle names, given at his christening.
explanation.definitionFit: Christening is when a child receives forenames, and these are the forenames the American poet Longfellow received.

clue.text: Keen on books in 10

indicators.note: the books are placed inside the figure

parts.note: the number 10 is read as the letters I and O
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A fan of reading inside a ten-letter answer.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a reference to the answer LIFE; it is the digits 1 and 0 read as the letters IO.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something is informal for being keen on it, enthusiastic about it.

clue.text: Mould upsets elephants

definitions.meaning: ... or musth is a frenzied state that seizes bull elephants

explanation.definitionFit: Must is an old word for mustiness or mould, and also the frenzy that grips male elephants.

clue.text: Singer said Roman officer made a big score

definitions.note: a verb phrase describing the person: one who has scored three hundred

parts.note: a treble is a boy singer with a high voice

indicators.note: said signals a word spoken aloud whose sound matches the entry

parts.note: a centurion commanded a hundred men in the Roman army

explanation.surface: A boy chorister talks of a Roman commander who racked up a great total.
explanation.walkthrough: A centurion in cricket scores a hundred; a treble one has scored 300.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has scored three centuries in one innings has made a very big score, three hundred runs.

clue.text: Spirit in the prophet Hosea

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: The animating spirit lives in the Old Testament prophet Hosea.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit of a community or culture.

clue.text: Brief visit gives Clare support

parts.note: Clare Short was a British Labour politician and cabinet minister
a stay is a support or prop

explanation.surface: A short trip gives a woman something to lean on.
explanation.walkthrough: Clare Short was a British Labour cabinet minister of the 1990s and 2000s.
explanation.definitionFit: A short stay is a brief visit, as in a short-stay car park.
